newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling stronger against the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling stronger against the dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling gained marginally against the dollar on Friday in a generally calm market, commercial dealers said.
"The shilling is stable. There is no high volatility, only a slight demand from one side. Some inflows are being seen from the coffee sector," a dealer at a leading bank told Reuters.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 56.43 against the dollar from 56.46 on Thursday. On the pound, it was posted at an average of 87.77 from 87.80 on Thursday.
"The market was generally very calm with little interest from large corporates," a dealer said. "The local unit maintained the levels of 56.40/55 against the dollar."
"Low importer demand vis a vis exporter inflows and the attractive shilling interest rates currently on offer continue to weigh heavily against any appreciation of the dollar," she said.
Another dealer added: "Today, being the last trading day of the week, the market may see great activity as players square their books."
Dealers said overnight money market rates maintained 22-24 percent levels as market liquidity was unchanged. The same levels should prevail in today's trade.
